speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the appearance of your skin lesions in detail, including their color, size, and any changes you've noticed over time. Are they itchy, painful, or bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of a non-healing lesion on your penis and another on your finger, along with your smoking history, is concerning. Have these lesions changed in size, developed a raised border, or begun to bleed spontaneously? Also, have you noticed any enlarged lymph nodes in your groin or armpit?

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of penile lesion; Biopsy of finger lesion.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopic images of both lesions.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy Findings: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. STD Panel: Syphilis Negative, HIV Negative, HBV Negative, HCV Negative. Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Dermatological Examination: Inspection shows an erythematous plaque with areas of crusting, oozing, and irregular borders on the dorsal surface of the penile shaft and the left middle finger. Palpation reveals lesions are firm, non-tender, with no warmth. Regional Lymph Nodes: No palpable cervical, axillary, or inguinal lymphadenopathy.
